Castle Ffrench on c.15.62 ha (c.39 acres)
Ballinamore Bridge, Co. Galway

“A Georgian manor house situated in a peaceful parkland setting.”

Location
Castle Ffrench is situated in the west of Ireland, c.5km from the village of Ballyforan. It has easy access to the provincial town of Athlone being c.25km away and the University City of Galway c.63km. Knock International Airport is c.70 km. Dublin is c.150km.

Description
This listed Grade ‘A’ manor house is set on c.39 acres of rolling parkland and is positioned a mile up a shared entrance appearing suddenly on arrival through century old trees. Consisting of three storeys over a basement, Castle Ffrench ranks amongst Ireland’s outstanding examples of Georgian architecture. It is absolutely one of a kind as seen by its original floor plan, elaborate plasterwork and woodwork. Further hallmarks of this country house are its ornate fireplaces and large bedrooms while eye-catching features also include a barrel-vaulted semi-basement, ornate cornicing, marble fireplaces, wooden floors and flag stoned hallway.

Outside there is a stone walled cobbled courtyard with outbuildings, a 2-bed apartment guest cottage, American barn with 16 stables and 8 paddocks.

Outbuildings and Land
Cobbled courtyard to rear of main house with attractive stone cottage divided into two apartments. The accommodation in both includes sitting room, kitchenette, bedroom and shower room. There is also a coach house, cow byre, storerooms with overhead loft and separate garage.

Beyond the courtyard there is an American Barn with 16 loose boxes, automated drinkers, feed / hay storage and overhead open loft.

The grounds total approximately 39 acres of which about 3 acres comprise of the gardens, yard and some woodland. The remaining 36 acres are situated to the front of the house. There is also a secondary access to the property via a cul de sac laneway off the L3210.

Services
Electricity, well water with treatment system and septic tank drainage.

History
Castle Ffrench was the ancestral home of the Ffrench family, one of the fourteen tribes of Galway. The house was built in 1779 by Sir Charles Ffrench, Mayor of Galway and was built on the site of an earlier castle.

Amenities
There is excellent hunting locally with the Galway Blazers, East Galway and North Galway hunts. There are golf courses nearby at Glassan and Athlone. The River Shannon, one of Europe’s longest navigable rivers is a short drive away. Lough Corrib internationally renowned for its Brown Trout fishing is within an hour’s drive of the property. The sandy beaches and majestic mountains of the west coast are within an easy drive.

Exclusions
Antique light in library and chandeliers in drawing room and dining room.
